17695-a-history-of-china-3d-ed-rev-and-e:
Wolfram Eberhard, of the University of California, wrote this history of China. It is a third edition, revised and enlarged, published in Berkeley and Los Angeles in 1969 by the University of California Press, with pictures. Earlier printings ran from 1955, with a second edition in 1960 and a reprint in 1966. Eberhard dedicates the book to his wife.

Contents open with an introduction and the earliest times, covering sources, Peking Man, and the Palaeolithic and Neolithic ages. Eight principal prehistoric cultures follow, with the Yang-shao and Lung-shan cultures named. Readers get a scholarly survey, sociological in outlook, still useful for early China.
a-history-of-china-3d-ed-rev-and-enl: The third edition, revised and enlarged, of Wolfram Eberhard's history of China updates his earlier work. Published by the University of California Press in 1969, it again opens with prehistory, Peking Man, and the great prehistoric cultures. Eberhard revised and reset the text for a new generation of readers. The edition remains a standard survey of Chinese history.

nasa-tm-19690021322-techniques-for-achie:
Wm. S. West of Goddard Space Flight Center served as technical officer for this April 1969 report, X-701-69-173. J. Michael L. Holman and Herbert W. Bilsky of RCA did the study under the NEW MOONS nuclear spacecraft evaluation. Their subject is magnetic cleanliness: keeping a deep-space craft's own magnetism from swamping the faint interplanetary fields its sensors must measure.

Missions to Jupiter and beyond frame the engineering problem throughout. The report gives methods and data for choosing a background interference allowance, illustrating with one-tenth of a gamma. Design, development, and test practices for craft and subsystems are covered in turn. Special magnetic problems raised by nuclear power supplies get their own treatment, with selected test data.
